1318: The cheap half of the Hex-9 line, with half the cache scraped off the die and sold anyway. {| Runs warm. | Sold by the tray. | Stamped, not tested.}
1319: The processor every office in the hyperpowers bought twice. {| Ceramic lid. | Batch number filed off. | Still the safe choice.}
1320: The first Omni-Lex part to reach a round thousand, and they never stopped saying so. {| The box shouts it. | A gigahertz of nothing much. | Worth it for the sticker.}
1321: A desktop part wedged into a portable, which is why it needs a fan and a prayer. {| Needs cooling. | Warps thin cases. | Drinks the battery.}
1322: Aokin built this one to sip rather than drink, and it shows in both directions. {| Barely warm. | Slow but patient. | Made for the road.}
1323: Crusader never won a benchmark and never lost a customer. {| Dull and dependable. | Warranty voided. | Second-hand, obviously.}
1324: Sixty-four megabytes, which was plenty until it very suddenly was not. {| Green board, gold teeth. | Pulled from something. | Add more.}
1325: The module everyone bought two of, because one was never the answer. {| Warm to the touch. | Sticker half peeled. | Buy two.}
1326: A quarter of a gigabyte, sold to people who said the word gigabyte a lot. {| Long and awkward. | EHI grade, no batch. | Wants a wide slot.}
1327: Double the data rate, double the price, roughly the same experience. {| The new standard. | Nobody can explain why. | Twice as fast, allegedly.}
1328: The most memory a sensible person owned in 2001, and it cost like it. {| Absurd capacity. | Priced by the megabyte. | Overkill, for now.}
1329: Pulled out of something older than the machine you are putting it into. {| Bent pin, straightened. | Smells faintly of smoke. | Free with anything.}
1330: Holds one and a bit megabytes and takes up a third of the case doing it. {| Clicks when idle. | Eats one disk in ten. | Nostalgic already.}
1331: Six gigabytes, spinning at four and a half thousand turns a minute in your lap. {| Warm as a cat. | Whines on seek. | Do not shake.}
1332: Twenty gigabytes, more than anyone could think of a use for. {| Roomy. | Ticks in the cold. | Half of it stays empty.}
1333: Suspended in rubber so it survives being dropped, which EHI expected. {| Rubber bumpers. | Heavy as a brick. | Rated for a fall.}
1334: No platters, no noise, and a price per megabyte that makes grown buyers wince. {| Silent. | Costs like jewellery. | Survives anything.}
1335: Burns six hundred and fifty megabytes at a time, and ruins one blank in five. {| Coasters, mostly. | Do not jog the table. | Loud on write.}
1336: Somebody else deleted everything on it, badly, and then threw it away. {| Clicks ominously. | Half the sectors answer. | Take it, please.}
1337: Enough to draw a desktop, and honest enough not to promise more. {| Flat colours only. | Draws windows. | Nothing fancy.}
1338: The one in every portable that claimed to do three dimensions and nearly did. {| Almost 3D. | Blurs at speed. | Good enough.}
1339: Genuinely draws triangles in hardware, and will tell you so on every boot. {| Real 3D, they insist. | Splash screen every time. | Gets hot.}
1340: More video memory than most machines have memory, which is the point. {| Absurdly overspecified. | Wants its own fan. | Shaped badly.}
1341: It turns numbers into a picture and refuses to be impressed by anything else. {| Sixteen colours. | Does the job. | Nothing more.}
1342: Four shades of grey, a ghost trailing every cursor, and a week of battery. {| Ghosting. | Readable in sunlight. | Lasts forever.}
1343: Colour at last, provided you look at it straight and do not move your head. {| Narrow viewing angle. | Washes out sideways. | Cheap colour.}
1344: An active matrix, which means every pixel gets its own transistor and its own opinion. {| One dead pixel. | Bright and even. | Worth the money.}
1345: Eight hundred by six hundred, and suddenly two windows fit side by side. {| Room to work. | Wants a big lid. | Perfectly even backlight.}
1346: The largest thing anyone has managed to hinge onto a handheld without it snapping. {| Enormous. | Flexes alarmingly. | Drains the cell.}
1347: A spidered corner and a dark stripe down the left, and it was free. {| Half the picture. | Free with the case. | Better than nothing.}
1348: Remembers the last time you charged it and refuses to go past that line again. {| Memory effect. | Heavy for the charge. | Cheap, at least.}
1349: Twice the charge of the old chemistry and none of the sulking. {| Self discharges. | Warm on the charger. | Honest work.}
1350: Lithium, light and eager, and best not punctured under any circumstances. {| Do not puncture. | Light for the charge. | Runs all day.}
1351: A flat slab that fills half the case and keeps the thing alive for two days. {| Fills the case. | Swells with age. | Two days of light.}
1352: A crust of salt around one terminal and about an hour in it, on a good day. {| Weeps quietly. | An hour, maybe. | Wear gloves.}
1353: Folds out into the light and gives back rather less than it promises. {| Needs real sun. | Awkward shape. | Never truly empty.}
1354: Screams at the exchange until the exchange screams back in the same key. {| Handshake noise. | Never quite 56k. | Ties up the line.}
1355: Works perfectly as long as nothing at all moves between the two eyes. {| Line of sight only. | Very slow. | Nobody uses it.}
1356: A card with a fragile little tongue of cable that everyone eventually snaps. {| Dongle always lost. | Faster than dialling. | Snaps at the neck.}
1357: Networking through the air, which nobody quite believes until they see it. {| Sorcery, surely. | Range of one room. | Eats the battery.}
1358: Puts the whole handheld on the telephone network, at a price per minute. {| Billed by the second. | Works anywhere. | Ruinously dear.}
1359: A flat plate that takes the heat off the chip and gives it to the case. {| Passive. | Gets the case hot. | Better than nothing.}
1360: Copper because copper works, and heavy because copper is heavy. {| Silent. | Weighs a lot. | Turns green in time.}
1361: Small enough to fit anywhere and loud enough to be heard from anywhere. {| Whines. | Fits everywhere. | Clogs with dust.}
1362: A sealed loop with a little fluid in it, doing quietly what a fan does badly. {| Bends around things. | Utterly silent. | Do not kink it.}
1363: Sixteen bits of sound, which is fifteen more than the machine strictly needs. {| Hisses. | Mono, really. | Enough for a beep.}
1364: Builds every instrument out of two sine waves shouting at each other. {| Everything sounds like brass. | Cheap and cheerful. | Very of its time.}
1365: Real recorded instruments, four kilobytes each, looped until they stop convincing. {| Audible loop point. | Nearly real. | Two megabytes of orchestra.}
1366: An ordinary die that spent a fortnight under a consecrated lamp and came back faster. {| Warm when unpowered. | Blessed at the fab. | Nobody will explain it.}
1367: The same dies as anyone else, with a binding cut into the substrate between them. {| Never faults. | Etching still glows. | Twice the density.}
1368: Couples straight into the ground current and never needs a telephone at all. {| No line rental. | Hums underfoot. | Works in caves.}
1369: Runs on a slow reaction in a sealed flask, and is refilled rather than recharged. {| Smells of vinegar. | Refill, not recharge. | Lasts a week.}
1370: An ordinary active matrix that occasionally renders something nobody sent it. {| Ghost frames. | Perfectly sharp. | Do not watch it idle.}
1371: A grown thing in a sealed cavity that holds whatever you last told it. {| Faint pulse. | Feed it monthly. | Remembers too well.}
1372: Layered metal and resin that takes the heat and declines to say where it goes. {| Cold to the touch. | Layered like a cake. | Ask no questions.}
1373: The housing of a hard drive with nothing inside it but a slow, steady turning. {| Weighs nothing. | Turns when unplugged. | Larger inside.}
1374: Six channels of synthesis, and a seventh that only appears after midnight. {| Counts to six. | Sings unprompted. | Beautiful, mostly.}
1375: Finishes frames the processor has not sent yet, and is usually right about them. {| Predictive. | Occasionally wrong. | Never stutters.}
1376: A single grown crystal that computes by ringing, and needs no current at all. {| Draws nothing. | Rings when working. | Cracks if dropped.}
1377: Hollow bone with something still written inside it, and room for a great deal more. {| Warm, always. | Never truly blank. | Do not bury it.}
1378: A jar of something cold and slightly luminous that gives up power very willingly. {| Cold to hold. | Faintly luminous. | Refills near graveyards.}
1379: Polished black glass that lights itself and needs nothing from the battery. {| No backlight needed. | Shows your face too. | Heavy as stone.}
1380: A live storm in a stoppered jar, which is exactly as sensible as it sounds. {| Crackles. | Recharge in rain. | Do not open.}
1381: A disc of vellum that holds everything ever written on it, and refuses deletion. {| Nothing is ever erased. | Smells of libraries. | Reads itself aloud.}
1382: Rings within rings that turn to work out the picture, and mutter while they do. {| Audible thinking. | Never needs power. | Turns on its own.}
1383: A closed ring of consecrated salt that heat declines to cross, along with other things. {| Sweeps clean nightly. | Keeps other things out. | Do not smudge it.}
1384: Forty small bells struck by forty small hammers, faster than the ear can follow. {| Rings constantly. | Needs no power. | Tunes itself.}
1385: Half a pair. Whatever reaches this stone left the other one a moment ago. {| No latency. | The other half is somewhere. | Listens both ways.}
1386: The last address writes into the first, so the module is always empty and always full. {| Full and empty at once. | Do not count it. | Ends where it begins.}
1387: Cultured nerve laid over a lattice, and it learns the work you give it. {| Twitches. | Gets faster with use. | Keep it damp.}
